author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces, the page and the machine-readable form, can be asked for the directory narrowed to a single whole specialty, matched without regard to letter case.
acceptance_criteria: The page surface at /vets.html accepts an optional specialty parameter and lists only veterinarians holding that specialty.
The machine-readable surface at /vets accepts the same optional specialty parameter and carries only veterinarians holding that specialty.
Matching is on the whole specialty name and disregards letter case; a value that is only part of a name matches no veterinarian.
A specialty no veterinarian holds returns the normal page or machine-readable document with an empty veterinarian list, not a failure.
A specialty value that is empty or all spaces behaves as if no filter were given, as the empty owner search does.
With no specialty value given, both surfaces behave exactly as they did before this slice.
Paging through a narrowed directory keeps the filter in force: the page links carry the specialty value.
A veterinarian holding several specialties is listed when the directory is narrowed to any one of them.
non_goals: A form, dropdown, or any other visible control for the filter on either surface
Free-text search for a veterinarian, a pet, or a visit
Managing veterinarians or their specialties (NG-2 stands)
Changing the shape of the machine-readable document beyond narrowing its veterinarian list
notes: Owner stated no further product answer will come; open choices took the narrowest reading and were recorded rather than consulted. Two open questions are now in docs/prd.md: whether either surface should gain a visible control, and whether a specialty value padded with spaces should be read as the name inside them. Narrowest reading taken for the padded value: it is matched as given against the whole specialty name, so it matches nobody; only an empty or all-spaces value counts as absent. Second narrowest reading: the machine-readable form keeps its current unpaged shape, paging applies to the page surface only. NG-9 is narrowed in docs/prd.md and recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-08-non-goal-veterinarian-specialty-filter.md; the ADR index row rides with it. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its identifier is not reused; its Superseded entry is amended to point at REQ-VET-003. No prd-autofix records existed to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends the vet feature package in place: no new package, no new pattern, no service layer. The narrowing is a Spring Data derived query on VetRepository over the Vet.specialties association, mirroring OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith. Two methods are needed, matching the two surfaces: a Page<Vet> variant for the paged /vets.html surface and a Collection<Vet> variant for the unpaged /vets surface, which keeps its current shape per the PRD. Case-insensitivity is expressed in the query (IgnoreCase), never by relying on vendor collation or a schema change. VetController gains an optional specialty @RequestParam on both handlers and chooses between the whole-directory and the narrowed repository call; that branch is request adaptation and route selection, not a business rule, so it does not extend the recorded Web-controller deviation (architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog, Web controller row). The matching rule itself lives in the query, where the catalog places it. One subtlety diverges from the owner-search seam and is easy to get wrong: OwnerController strips the search value, but the PRD's narrowest reading for this slice says a padded specialty value matches nobody while an all-spaces value counts as absent. The controller therefore tests the raw value with isBlank() to decide absence and passes the raw, unstripped value to the query when present. Durable-memory writes: the Contracts rows for VetController, VetRepository, and Vets now carry REQ-VET-003; the Known Defects row calling the machine-readable route 'pending removal' is removed, since the route is a supported surface under this requirement; docs/system-design.md section Persistence records that narrowed reads are uncached and that case folding lives in the query; a new ADR carries the why.
integration_points: Repository boundary, matching semantics: a REAL VetRepository under @DataJpaTest against seeded H2, in a new src/test/java/.../vet/VetRepositoryTests.java. No double. The case-insensitive whole-name rule lives inside the derived query, so a stub would only re-implement and then confirm itself. Seeded H2 data supports every case: Helen Leary and Henry Stevens hold radiology, Rafael Ortega holds surgery, Linda Douglas holds surgery and dentistry (the multi-specialty case), James Carter and Sharon Jenkins hold none.

Repository boundary, controller wiring: the existing Mockito @MockitoBean VetRepository in VetControllerTests stays and gains stubbings for the new methods. Reason neither a real nor a hand-written implementation fits: @WebMvcTest loads no persistence context, and a hand-written in-memory double would have to re-implement the matching rule the query owns. These tests assert parameter binding, branch selection, model contents, and the rendered paging links only, never the matching rule.
Framework transport: MockMvc, the project's one sanctioned mock, for both /vets.html and /vets.

Place the new file at vet/VetRepositoryTests.java rather than extending service/ClinicServiceTests.java. ClinicServiceTests is the @DataJpaTest precedent for real repository reads, but its package implies a clinic-service concept the application does not have (ubiquitous-language.md, naming collisions). Feature-package placement matches ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization.
The Vets wrapper's serialized shape does not change; only which veterinarians it carries.

patterns.description: derived paged query taking a search value plus Pageable, the shape the narrowed vet query follows
controller normalizing an absent or blank search value before choosing the repository call; follow the branch, not the .strip() (see the padded-value rule in architectural_fit)
@DataJpaTest exercising the real VetRepository against seeded H2 — the precedent the new VetRepositoryTests follows
the paging block to extend so every link carries the specialty value

risks.risk: Copying the template's existing @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} preprocessing style for the specialty value places request-derived text into an href without URL encoding, giving a reflected injection point in a rendered attribute.
risks.mitigation: Use the Thymeleaf link-expression parameter form, @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}, which encodes every parameter. Converting the whole paging block to that form is preferred over mixing styles (security-principles.md § Realization, Cross-site scripting row).

risks.risk: Annotating the new repository methods @Cacheable("vets") would key an unbounded, never-evicting cache by caller-supplied text — a memory-exhaustion vector in a demonstration that readers copy.
risks.mitigation: The new methods carry no cache annotation; the two whole-directory methods keep theirs unchanged. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-08-specialty-filtered-vet-reads-are-not-cached.md and in docs/system-design.md § Persistence.

risks.risk: Expressing case-insensitivity through vendor collation or a schema change repeats the PostgreSQL owner-search defect, where the same search returns different results per database.
risks.mitigation: Fold case in the derived query (IgnoreCase). No schema file changes (docs/system-design.md § Known Defects, PostgreSQL owner search row).

risks.risk: The join through the @ManyToMany specialties association can return duplicate Vet rows and skew Page.getTotalElements().
risks.mitigation: A single equality predicate yields at most one join row per veterinarian, so duplicates are not expected. The @DataJpaTest asserts the exact result set and the page total; if duplicates appear, add Distinct to the derived method name.

risks.risk: Writing all eight acceptance criteria as MockMvc tests against the stubbed repository would assert the stub's answers and prove nothing about case-insensitivity, whole-name matching, or the multi-specialty case.
risks.mitigation: Split by boundary as the integration_points prescribe: matching semantics in VetRepositoryTests against real H2, wiring and rendering in VetControllerTests (testing-principles.md § mocking policy).

risks.risk: Adding a visible filter control, or a form-backed search, would breach the PRD non-goal and the recorded product decision.
risks.mitigation: The filter is a URL contract only. The template gains parameter-carrying links and nothing else (prd.md NG-9 as narrowed; ADR 2026-09-08-non-goal-veterinarian-specialty-filter).

notes: No design-doc-autofix records existed to audit. Open question recorded rather than consulted, per the owner's standing instruction: the PRD's padded-value question is unresolved, and this block pins the narrowest reading (isBlank decides absence; a present value is matched unstripped). If the reviewer or implementer finds that reading unworkable, raise a consultation-request rather than stripping silently. The machine-readable surface stays unpaged, so /vets takes specialty but not page. Requirement ids joined the Contracts rows for VetController, VetRepository, and Vets for the contracts-sync gate.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this review: build.gradle declares no OWASP dependencyCheck plugin, so dependencyCheckAnalyze could not run and this reviewer has no network access. The change itself alters no dependency (build.gradle is not in the change set), so the surface is unchanged; a human or CI should close the standing NVD check for Spring Boot 4.1.1 separately from this slice.

The specialty parameter has no explicit length bound before it reaches the derived query. Harm is limited (the value is parameterized, uncached, and bounded by the container's request-line limit), so this is not a defect on this change; if a future slice caches or logs the value, add an explicit bound at the boundary first.

Neither /vets.html nor /vets gained a filter form or an allowlist of known specialty names. Matching arbitrary caller text against Specialty.name is safe as written, but an allowlist drawn from the specialties table would narrow the boundary further if the filter later feeds anything beyond the query.
approved_aspects: Data-access injection: the specialty filter reaches the database only through Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, both overloads). No string-concatenated query text, no @Query, no createQuery/createNativeQuery anywhere in the vet package. Satisfies security-principles.md 'Injection into data access'.

XSS: the request-derived specialty is never rendered as text or markup. Its only template use is as a link-expression parameter (@{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${filter})}), which URL-encodes the value and HTML-escapes the rendered href; th:with only calls String.isEmpty() on it. Default output escaping is untouched, no th:utext added.

Template-expression injection: the change replaces the pre-existing preprocessing links (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}) with link expressions. Request-derived text therefore never enters a __${...}__ preprocessing slot. Swept the rest of src/main/resources/templates/: the remaining preprocessing sites (layout.html:31, inputField/selectField fragments, ownerDetails, ownersList) are pre-existing and interpolate fragment-local names and entity identifiers, not request-supplied text.

Caching: VetRepository documents the deliberate omission of @Cacheable on both new finders, so caller-supplied text never becomes an unbounded cache key. The divergence from the @Cacheable("vets") neighbour carries its inline justification, meeting the Pattern Consistency clause.

Exposed surface unchanged: no new endpoint. /vets.html and /vets each gain one optional scalar @RequestParam; both were already unauthenticated in the recorded demonstration baseline (system-design.md Security Context), and neither mutates state. No management-endpoint exposure change.
Mass assignment: specialty binds as a scalar @RequestParam, not into a command object, so no new binder and no identifier-binding surface.

Null and type safety: requestedSpecialty() handles the absent and blank parameter at the boundary and returns a non-null empty string, so the downstream isEmpty() calls and the template's specialty.isEmpty() cannot NPE. No raw types, no unguarded casts, no Optional.get().

Controller and repository remain stateless singletons; no mutable shared state, no SimpleDateFormat, no executors, no file or network I/O, no logging added, no secrets in the diff (grepped the change set for password/secret/token/key/credential: zero hits).
No new or changed dependency: build.gradle is outside the change set, so this change adds no supply-chain surface.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty

blast_radius.note: Contained to the vet package in one module: two controller routes, two derived repository methods, and the vetList paging links, plus documentation. No sensitive or security-surface paths, and the 41 hunks are almost all small and local to the vet slice.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every production hunk and found no hidden behavior change: the no-filter path still calls findAll, the empty-string sentinel from requestedSpecialty is set on the model before the template dereferences it, and the paging links were rewritten from string preprocessing to a link expression whose empty-list idiom drops the parameter entirely, so unfiltered URLs keep their old shape. The join-on-specialties paging count, the classic trap here, is pinned against the real database.

test_adequacy.note: The matching rule is tested against a real repository and the seeded database rather than a double, asserting real outcomes on the boundaries that matter: whole-name-only, case folding, padded values, a specialty nobody holds, a vet under each of several specialties, and the paged total counting only holders. Controller tests drive the rendered page and assert the paging link carries the filter and drops it when none was asked for.

reviewer_hedging.note: Three of the four round-1 approvals carry a recommendations list rather than approving bare. The security reviewer's is the one worth reading: the caller-supplied specialty reaches the derived query with no explicit length bound, judged safe only because the value is parameterized, uncached and unlogged, and the standing NVD supply-chain check could not be run here. Test review flagged that the blank-value branch is never driven through the machine-readable route, and code quality flagged the two-line filter branch duplicated once per route.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions, and the diff matches the triaged surface. The documentation reach beyond the file targets, two ADRs plus the NG-9 narrowing and the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 amendment, is how the recorded scope override was required to be recorded.

rationale: The code reads clean and the tests are real, including the join-paging count against a live database. What earns a closer look is the reviewers' fine print, not the diff: an unbounded caller-supplied string reaching the query, an unrun supply-chain check, and an untested blank-value path on the JSON route. Read those three notes, then merge.
